question: Who became the first athlete in history to run sub-10 s in the 100 m for 11 consecutive years?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Akani Simbine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **South African** sprinter **Akani Simbine** made history in **July 2024** by becoming the first athlete to record sub-10 second times in the **100m** for **11 consecutive years**.
 
• He achieved this milestone at the **London Diamond League** held at the **London Stadium**, where he clocked a season-best time of **9.86 seconds**.
 
• This remarkable streak began in **2014** when he first broke the **10-second barrier**, and he has maintained this world-class performance level every single year through **2024**.
 
• By reaching 11 consecutive years, he officially surpassed the previous record of **9 consecutive years** held by the legendary **Jamaican** sprinter **Usain Bolt**, who maintained his streak from **2008 to 2016**. ***Hence, the statement regarding his record-breaking consistency is correct.***
 
• The **Diamond League** performance in **2024** served as a crucial warm-up for the **Paris 2024 Olympics**, reinforcing his status as one of the most consistent sprinters in athletic history. ***Hence, Akani Simbine is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Akani Simbine:**
 
 
• Born on **21 September 1993** in **Johannesburg, South Africa**, Simbine is a specialist in the **100 meters** sprint.
 
• He is the **South African national record holder** in the 100m and has consistently finished in the top 5 at major championships, including the **Tokyo 2020** and **Paris 2024 Olympics**.
 
• His career is defined by extreme consistency, having reached the finals of the **World Athletics Championships** and **Olympic Games** multiple times since **2016**.
 
 
 
• **Usain Bolt:**
 
 
• An **eight-time Olympic gold medalist**, Bolt is the world record holder in the **100m (9.58s)** and **200m (19.19s)**.
 
• While he is considered the greatest sprinter of all time, his streak of sub-10 second finishes lasted **9 years**, ending with his retirement in **2017**.
 
 
 
• **Trayvon Bromell:**
 
 
• An **American** sprinter who was the first high school athlete to break the 10-second barrier.
 
• Although he has recorded extremely fast times, including a personal best of **9.76 seconds**, his career has been plagued by **Achilles tendon injuries**, preventing a long consecutive yearly streak.
 
 
 
• **Andre De Grasse:**
 
 
• A **Canadian** sprinter and the **2020 Olympic 200m champion**.
 
• Known as a "big-game performer," De Grasse has won numerous medals at the **Olympics** and **World Championships**, but his sub-10 second performances in the 100m have not occurred in **11 consecutive years**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **sub-10 second barrier** is a historical hallmark of elite sprinting. While many athletes have achieved it, maintaining the physical condition to do so annually for over a decade is rare due to the high risk of **injuries** and **age-related** physiological declines.
 
• **Asafa Powell**, another **Jamaican** legend, holds the record for the **most total sub-10 second clockings** in history (97 times), but Simbine’s record focuses on the **consecutive nature** of the years in which the feat was achieved.
 
• The **World Athletics** governing body tracks these statistics to highlight longevity in the sport, where **Akani Simbine** now stands as the benchmark for sustained excellence in the **100m dash**.
 
• Simbine's 2024 season also saw him anchor the **South African 4x100m relay team** to a **Silver Medal** at the **Paris 2024 Olympics**, further cementing his legacy in **African athletics**.
